# Question: How much did the congestion charge reduce traffic and pollution in the central zone?

## Answer
The congestion charge cut weekday traffic in the central zone by 25 percent [S1]. Bus journey times in the zone fell by 6 percent [S1].

## Evidence
- Air pollution near zone boundaries fell by 12 percent in the first year [S2].
- The transport department says the charge cut weekday traffic in the central zone by up to 25 percent at peak hours [S1].
- A review found that air pollution near zone boundaries fell by between 8 and 12 percent in the first year [S2].
- Daily cyclists entering the zone rose to 14,000 [S2].

## Counter-evidence and limits
- The review covered 40 monitoring stations [S2].
- Effects outside peak hours are not reported by these sources (judgment)

## Next actions
- Ask the transport department for the average reduction across all hours (judgment)

## Sources
- [S1] Transport department congestion charge results
- [S2] Air quality and cycling review
